## Valuation & Funding

HappyRobot closed a $44 million Series B round in September 2025 led by Base10 Partners at approximately $500 million valuation.
The round included participation from existing investors Andreessen Horowitz and Y Combinator, along with new backers Tokio Marine, WaVe-X, and World Innovation Lab.

The company previously raised a $15.6 million Series A in December 2024 led by Andreessen Horowitz. Earlier funding included participation from Y Combinator, Array Ventures, Samsara Ventures, and RyderVentures.

HappyRobot has raised nearly $62 million total since its founding in 2022.

## Product

HappyRobot operates as an AI-native operating system that lets logistics companies build custom AI workers to handle routine communication and operational tasks. Think of it as a drag-and-drop factory where freight brokers, 3PLs, and shippers can create digital teammates that speak on phones, write emails, parse documents, and browse web portals while keeping humans in the loop.

# HappyRobot Raises $44 Million in Series B

HappyRobot, a San Francisco, CA-based AI automation company, has raised $44 million in Series B funding, bringing its total funding to $62 million.

Ben Murray profile image

by Ben Murray

Updated September 04, 2025

HappyRobot, a San Francisco, CA-based AI automation company, has raised $44 million in Series B funding, bringing its total funding to $62 million.

## Investors

The round was led by Base10 Partners, with participation from Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Y Combinator, Tokio Marine, WaVe-X, and World Innovation Lab (WiL).

Base10 Partners is a venture capital firm founded in 2017 and headquartered in San Francisco, California. The firm focuses on investing in early-stage companies that bring automation to traditional sectors of the economy, which it refers to as the “automation of the real economy.” It primarily invests in companies applying automation to industries such as finance, food, healthcare, retail, logistics, and construction.

## HappyRobot Use of Funds
The company will use the funds to hire top talent, enhance its AI platform, and expand enterprise deployments.

## About HappyRobot

Founded in 2023, HappyRobot is an AI-native operating system designed to orchestrate autonomous AI workers capable of handling tasks across businesses, with a particular focus on the logistics and supply chain industries. Its AI agents integrate transcription, LLMs, voice generation, OCR, and browser automation, with deep integrations into systems such as TMS, ERP, and CRM. The company serves more than 70 enterprise customers, including DHL, Ryder, Schneider, and Werner. Headquartered in San Francisco, its mission is to build the AI operating system for the real economy.

# HappyRobot Raises $150m in Funding to Grow Agent Deployment

By Louise Collins

August 06, 2026

undefined mins

Share this article

**Prioritise Us** on Google

Share this article

**Prioritise Us** on Google

HappyRobot is expanding its global operations with its latest round of funding. Credit: HappyRobot

Software start-up company HappyRobot has raised US$150m in Series C funding, accelerating its global go-to-market growth and AI agent deployment

As global supply chains become increasingly complex, AI models are becoming more necessary.

HappyRobot helps global enterprises use agents to overcome this complexity, deployed across [core business functions](https://aimagazine.com/ai-applications/how-workdays-new-system-manages-ai-human-workforce) in order to drive efficiency.

In a Series C round of funding, it has raised US$150m, having grown dramatically since its foundation in 2023.

Youtube Placeholder

...

Having successfully tackled the complex and operationally demanding sector of logistics, it is getting ready to aid organisations in telecommunications, insurance, airlines and energy and utilities.

With the scale it can now grow to due to its recent funding, it can offer its support across any sector or organisation where fragmented systems are hindering seamless operations.

"What started as a voice agent deployed in a US freight broker two years ago has grown into a full Enterprise AI platform deployed in over 150 enterprises globally across supply chain, energy and utilities, telecom, insurance and airlines," Pablo Palafox, CEO at HappyRobot, said on LinkedIn.

Pablo Palafox, CEO of HappyRobot

"We’ve grown 5x since our Series B and continue to work hard towards our vision of Enterprise Superintelligence: the state where an organisation's collective intelligence compounds as [agents and humans](https://technologymagazine.
com/articles/the-rise-of-home-robots-impact-on-technology-sector) learn from one another.

"And it starts by deploying your first agent. Much like that first agent we deployed two years ago."

## The Series C round

This Series C [funding](https://supplychaindigital.com/news/freehand-scaling-ai-across-the-supply-chain-with-75m-fund) was led by Prysm Capital and co-led by Eurazeo, with further support from existing investors a16z, Base10, and Y Combinator. It has also been helped by Koch Disruptive Technologies (KDT), Kfund, Orange, T.Capital (Deutsche Telekom), Bankinter, Endeavor Catalyst and Wave-X.

Due to this funding round, the start-up has now been valued at US$1.2bn post-money, with a total funding of approximately US$200m. The company is entering a new stage of growth, sending its AI agents out across the industry as [complexity becomes a constant](https://supplychaindigital.com/articles/navigating-global-complexity-with-third-party-logistics) .
"Many industries have a surprising share of their costs locked up in coordination, the calls, emails and handoffs that keep work flowing," says Kerry Wei, Partner at Prysm Capital.

Kerry Wei, Partner at Prysm Capital

"While getting an agent to complete a discrete task is increasingly simple, deploying them across multi-step enterprise workflows has proven far more difficult. HappyRobot has built the missing link – the governance, interfaces and context layer – that enables agents to work seamlessly across complex workflows, driving real ROI by allowing companies to capture value without asking employees to adopt anything new.

"We were blown away by what Pablo and the team already have running in production, and by the boldness of their vision. We are thrilled to partner with the team we believe is positioned to redefine how enterprise operations get done."

## Meeting industry complexity
Despite the complexity that modern supply chains are facing, many organisations are still using fragmented systems, either having avoided the digitalisation journey entirely or not quite hit the mark. Every day, operations are taking place through spreadsheets, outdated documents, emails and phone calls. With this, many organisations have failed to automate their workflows, instead using manual processes which take much longer, are more prone to mistakes and are less efficient.

HappyRobot deploys [AI agents](https://procurementmag.com/technology-and-ai/cognizant-will-take-enterprises-next-generation-ai) which can work alongside employees and execute tasks. Each month, HappyRobot's customers are seeing measurable impact, with ongoing deployments throughout the course of a partnership. At each stage of deployment, agents are refined to ensure they are flexible and adaptable to modern needs.

HappyRobot has raised US$150m in Series C funding. Credit: HappyRobot
"Getting agents to do work is the starting point, not the destination," explains Pablo.

"Our thesis is that enterprise superintelligence, where an organisation's collective intelligence compounds as agents and people learn from one another, requires far more than task-performing agents. It requires a platform and a deployed motion capable of operationalising that platform inside a specific business."

HappyRobot's customers' operational teams have grown their capacity by 10x, with fives times more revenue being generated by sales teams. HappyRobot is unlocking new value and finding underutilised channels in order to help customers with efficiency and growth. This new funding will expand its capabilities and allow it to integrate further within the supply chain.
